title: Latency-first phase aligner for multi-GPU prefill and decode
creator: Jordan Lee
description:
Problem: In multi-GPU inference for large models we observe p50 latency improvements from batching but p99 regressions during prefill->decode transitions due to poor alignment of NCCL collective windows and stage handoffs. Existing schedulers either prioritize throughput (large batching) or conservative synchronization (serial prefill then decode) which increases tail latency under bursty request patterns.

Goal: Implement a latency-first phase alignment layer (PhaseAligner) that dynamically establishes short deterministic micro-batching windows and phase boundaries across tensor- and pipeline-parallel stages so NCCL all-reduces and attention KV prefill can overlap with decode when safe. The feature should reduce p99 token latency for mixed prefill/decode workloads while retaining >90% of baseline throughput and providing runtime fallbacks for noisy hardware or stragglers.

Scope: 1) Kernel-level hooks to mark fusion-safe attention compute so KV cache writes can be scheduled earlier. 2) A coordination protocol between stage leaders (tensor/pipeline) to reserve micro-window boundaries and emit soft barriers instead of hard syncs. 3) Opportunistic NCCL overlap: start non-blocking collectives earlier when downstream readiness probability exceeds threshold. 4) Telemetry and rollout: tracing, microbench dashboards, and canary rollout with automatic fallback to previous scheduler on regression.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Aggressive overlap reduces latency but can increase GPU memory pressure (prefill writes earlier); mitigations: dynamic window sizing and memory watermarks.
- Adding leader coordination increases control-plane messages; mitigations: lightweight gRPC control plane on local host, piggyback on existing conductor heartbeats.
- Risk of correctness/regression when kernels reorder side-effecting ops; mitigations: conservative kernel tagging and verification tests.

Implementation outline: 
- PhaseAligner core: C++ component in runtime orchestration layer that negotiates micro-window length and alignment offsets per workload class.
- Kernel annotations: extend kernel registry to expose "safe-early-kv-flush" tag and latency-cost estimate.
- NCCL strategy: non-blocking IAllReduce with a small completion check window and fallback to blocking if completion stalls beyond threshold.
- Canary flow: runtime flag runtime.phase_aligner=canary with percentile-based regression checks against runtime.console metrics.

Performance targets: 
- Reduce p99 token latency by >=20% on mixed prefill(>128 tokens)/decode workloads for 8xA100 pools.
- Maintain throughput >=90% of baseline under steady-state batching.
- No correctness regressions across test suite (unit + model replay).
acceptance_criteria: PhaseAligner builds and can be enabled via runtime flag without restarting worker processes
End-to-end canary on internal perf harness shows >=15% p99 reduction for target workload on 8-GPU topology within 2 weeks of rollout
Fall-back path reliably disables overlap on memory pressure or >2x expected NCCL stall and returns metrics to previous baseline
Kernel registry has 'safe-early-kv-flush' annotations for at least 3 attention kernel variants and unit tests validating ordering semantics
Instrumentation emits per-request phase boundary traces (start/align/commit) which are visualized in console runbook dashboard
reproduction_steps: Checkout branch feature/phase-aligner and build runtime: cmake -B build -S . && ninja -C build
Start 8xA100 multi-GPU emulation cluster using dev-env scripts: ./dev/setup_mgpu.sh --topology 8xA100
Compare runtime.console p50/p95/p99 traces against baseline run with runtime.phase_aligner=off
Inspect NCCL traces and kernel timing via /tmp/runtime-traces/*.trace and the perf dashboard link below
comments: 2025-02-15 Jordan Lee: Initial spike completed. Found that attention kernel A has safe reorder properties for KV writes when residuals are not mutated. Prototype kernel tag in repo at //runtime/kernel_registry.cc:PR#1243.

2025-02-18 Priya Menon: Implemented a lightweight leader elector using host-local IPC to avoid extra RPCs; pushed design doc to Confluence (link below). Planning to prototype non-blocking IAllReduce next week.

2025-02-20 Ravi Patel (review): Concern about memory pressure when early KV flushes accumulate. Suggest adding per-stage memory watermark and an adaptive shrink of micro-window. Filed ENG-33179 as follow-up for memory watermarks.
2025-02-24 QA Bot: Canary run failed on nightly with a rare NCCL stall; stack traces attached to GH-PR#1278. Reverting to canary=false until mitigation implemented. Priya to triage.

2025-02-26 Priya Menon: Mitigation implemented: backoff timer + health probe before starting collectives. Re-ran canary; preliminary numbers show p99 down by 18% on synthetic workload. Collecting longer runs for stability metrics.
